name: Isomorphic Labs
blurb: Alphabet's AI drug design company and its funding.
title: Isomorphic Labs
answer: Isomorphic Labs was spun out of Google DeepMind to turn AlphaFold class models into a drug design engine. It has partnerships with major drugmakers and has raised $600 million in 2025 and a further $2.1 billion in 2026 to scale the engine and take its own candidates into the clinic.

reading.body:
Isomorphic Labs raised $600 million in 2025 and $2.1 billion in 2026 to scale an AI drug design engine spun out of Google DeepMind.

The two rounds are a year apart and the second is more than three times the first. That is the shape of a company moving from proving a design engine works to paying for the work of pushing its own candidates into clinical trials. The stated uses match: the 2025 round funded engine development and early programmes, the 2026 round funds scale and pipeline progression.

The relevance to AI is that this is a pure test of whether structure based models produce molecules that survive contact with patients. The data records partnerships with major drugmakers but names none of them and gives no trial dates, so the clinical readout is still ahead. The first clinical data is the event that will settle the question.

What the data does not cover is compute. No chip counts, no data centre capacity, no training run sizes appear here, so nothing in this record supports a claim about how much compute the engine consumes or where it runs. It also gives no headcount, no valuation, and no breakdown of how the $2.7 billion across both rounds is allocated.

explainer:
Isomorphic Labs was founded in 2021 by Demis Hassabis as a sister company to Google DeepMind, with the aim of turning advances in protein structure prediction into a general engine for designing medicines. It co-developed AlphaFold 3 with DeepMind and has used its models to work on its own internal programmes and with pharmaceutical partners.

Its funding marks how much the market expects from structure based AI design. The company raised 600 million dollars in 2025, its first outside funding, and a further 2.1 billion dollars in 2026. Like other AI drug designers it ultimately has to prove itself in the clinic, where molecules designed with its engine will be judged by the same standards as any other drug candidate.
